extracted.intended_audience: scientists and researchers (plant pathologists, bacteriologists, astronomers/instrumentalists, aeronautical scientists, psychologists, and archaeologists) — readers of Nature
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing methodological, observational, and instrument-design standards and requirements as discussed in short research notes and letters (e.g., plant‑pathology observations, interferometer design, motorless flight theory, psychophysical experiments, archaeological authentication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Control comparison with killed host tissue for infection studies
rubrics_metrics.description: No rise of temperature was observed when the host tissue was killed prior to inoculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include killed-tissue controls when investigating temperature changes in infected living tissue to distinguish host reaction from purely physical/chemical effects of the pathogen or inoculum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument sensitivity for measuring temperature changes in infected tissue
rubrics_metrics.description: Mercury-in-glass thermometers were used in making these observations, but the employment of thermo-electric apparatus will naturally be necessary to carry the investigations further.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with practical instruments but adopt more sensitive/suitable apparatus (e.g., thermoelectric sensors) for finer measurements and for advancing the investigation beyond preliminary observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinded placebo/control mixtures in drug-effect experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: He disguised the drug, and prepared a control mixture which was indistinguishable from it. On certain days the drug mixture was taken, on other days the control mixture was taken, the subject never knowing which he was drinking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disguise active treatments and provide indistinguishable control mixtures so subjects are unaware of condition, to control for suggestion, interest, and placebo effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding withdrawal confounds by long cessation before substance experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: He found that the sudden cessation of all tea and coffee necessary for the study of the effects of caffeine induced a loss of energy... Therefore most of his experiments were carried out more than twelve months after the taking of these drinks had been discontinued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow substantial washout periods (the author reports conducting experiments more than twelve months after cessation) to avoid confounds from withdrawal or recent use when studying drug or stimulant effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured repeated-measure protocol for ergographic (fatigue) studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of recording a single ergogram Rivers took several sets of ergograms each day, each set consisting usually of six ergograms taken at intervals of two minutes, and separated from the next set by an interval of thirty or sixty minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple repeated measures within sessions and spaced sets across the day to characterise performance/fatigue reliably rather than relying on single recordings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insistence on precise scientific procedure and critical scrutiny of methods
rubrics_metrics.description: His insistence on scientific procedure, his delight in scientific analysis... devotion to scientific methods and accuracy could not fail to advance the subject. He felt instinctively that many of the supposed effects of alcohol were really due to the suggestion, interest, excitement or sensory stimulation accompanying the taking of the drug.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experiments to eliminate artefacts and suggestibility; critically assess and correct faulty methods; value methodological rigor and disguised controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative/field psychophysical methods: systematic application of apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: This was the first expedition in which systematic work was carried out in the ethnological application of the methods and apparatus of experimental psychology... His psychological investigations among the Torres Straits islanders, Egyptians and Todas ... will ever stand as models of precise, methodical observations in the field of ethnological psychology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the same experimental apparatus and methods systematically across field populations; measure comparable variables (visual acuity, colour vision, susceptibility to illusions) and document sampling and procedures carefully for cross-population comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archaeological authentication requires in-situ evidence and field testing
rubrics_metrics.description: We cannot use suspect material as evidence, and the best thing to do is to go into the field and test it. If Mr. Armstrong will find a site where flint flakes and implements are to be found under the peat in sufficient numbers to justify digging, I will come and bring a spade with me.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept surface‑found or dubiously‑provenanced artefacts as evidence; verify authenticity through controlled excavation, looking for associated artefacts and stratigraphic context beneath peat or deposits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design specifications and principles for a large Michelson stellar interferometer
rubrics_metrics.description: My specifications ... call for a light but very rigid skeleton girder about 54 feet long and 10 feet deep at its centre ... bolted to a heavy plate carried by the upper extremity of the polar axis ... paraboloidal mirror of 36 inches aperture and about 15 feet focal length ... two outer plane mirrors, each 15 inches in diameter, mounted at 45° on carriages which slide along rails ... distance between these mirrors, when the fringes disappear completely, gives the angular diameter of the star if the mean wave-length of its light is known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When scaling interferometers, balance optical/design goals with cost: use a rigid but light skeleton girder, mount optical elements to allow adjustment, design polar axis through centre of gravity, provide range of RA motion (~14 hours each way), and measure fringe visibility/vanishing baseline to derive angular diameters (with known mean wavelength).

rubrics_metrics.name: Optical alignment and path-length compensation techniques for interferometers
rubrics_metrics.description: The rails, carefully planed in 12-foot lengths ... will be optically lined up by adjusting screws. The final compensation for length of path will be effected by a sliding wedge, of the type designed by Prof. Michelson for the 20-foot interferometer. Comparison fringes, adjustable for visibility, will be provided as an aid to the observer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use modular planed rails aligned optically with adjusting screws; provide a sliding-wedge delay for final optical-path compensation and adjustable comparison fringes to aid fringe visibility assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engineering simplification and use of standard parts to reduce instrument cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the design precautions have been taken to reduce the amount of large and expensive machine work to a minimum. The girder need be only approximately straight, as the rails ... will be optically lined up by adjusting screws. ... built of standard steel shapes, cut to length at the mill and riveted together on Mount Wilson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimise bespoke machining by using standard steel shapes, modular construction, and alignment adjustments in situ to lower construction cost without sacrificing required optical performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay further instrumental developments until adequate experience with smaller prototypes
rubrics_metrics.description: It was also thought advisable to postpone further instrumental developments until they could be undertaken in the light of prolonged experience with the 20-foot interferometer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validate techniques and operational procedures on smaller existing instruments before committing to larger, costlier constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical criteria for sustained motorless (wind-) flight
rubrics_metrics.description: The wind is indeed the main instrument of motorless flight... the wind must be upwards or unsteady in order to supply this energy... a steady horizontal wind cannot make the machine stay at the same level in the air for any length of time, or climb. If the wind is steady, but has an upward component, it helps in the attainment of real flight...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims or demonstrations of sustained motorless flight must show either an upward component of wind or unsteady/variable wind (gusts, rising/retarding wind) that can provide energy; steady horizontal wind alone cannot sustain flight without an engine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative relation between glider glide characteristics and wind components
rubrics_metrics.description: If a glider ... performs a straight line glide with speed U at gliding angle θ below the horizontal, then a steady wind of speed U, blowing at an angle θ above the horizontal, will keep the glider suspended in the air indefinitely, if it points into the wind... more generally, if U' sin θ' = U sin θ then the machine will fly horizontally ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the derived relations (vertical components of wind matching the glider's sink rate) to predict when a given glider and wind vector can sustain level flight or climb; provide such quantitative checks when asserting wind‑flight performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research agenda for motorless flight (three priorities)
rubrics_metrics.description: The future of wind-flight is associated with three main lines of study: (1) The motions that are continually taking place in the atmosphere ... the 'internal structure of the wind.' (2) Motorless flight presents problems of design ... Stability is essential, but easy control is a sine qua non. (3) The rigid dynamics of wind‑flight ... the pilot must make use of any stray wind that comes to his aid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise (1) detailed study of atmospheric microstructure and unsteady flows, (2) glider design that emphasises lightness, stability and rapid controllability, and (3) dynamic/rigid-body analysis of unsteady flight to guide pilot technique and machine design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for observational reporting of transient luminous phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: While standing about twenty yards from the sea‑shore ... Time, 7.15 P.M.; wind strong from the west, bringing up a good deal of low cloud and very fine rain in the air causing bad visibility; sea rather rough with four lines of breakers at the shore... The appearances of the light were not the same to my wife as to myself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record precise observational metadata (time, weather, wind direction, visibility, sea state, angular extent/elevation) and multiple independent observer impressions; use environmental data to rule out candidate causes (e.g., distant lightning) and consider retinal/psychophysical explanations.
